title: EU must avoid 'risky dependencies' in critical technologies, digital chief says
source_used: European Newsroom interview with Henna Virkkunen (MLex page paywalled; only its description readable)
key_facts: MLex description: avoiding risky dependencies in critical technologies (AI, quantum computing, semiconductors, space, cyber security) is one of the top goals for Henna Virkkunen, the Commission's digital chief, who said in an interview that the AI Act is a good model for global AI regulation.

European Newsroom (9 Oct 2026): Virkkunen said the Union should avoid dependence on a single company or third country for critical technologies and develop AI based on European values, languages and culture.
She said the Commission has sent Requests for Information (formal fact-gathering) to OpenAI, Anthropic and unnamed Chinese companies.
She warned of a 'risk of very serious incidents' without guardrails and called for international safeguards.
The EU began enforcing its AI Act in August.
quote_evidence: Ensuring that the EU doesn't have risky dependencies in critical technologies — AI, quantum computing, semiconductors, space and cyber security — is one of the top goals for Henna Virkkunen, the European Commission's digital chief said in an interview.
I'm sure that all those countries who are not willing to regulate the use of AI, they will come back to that quite soon.
why_it_matters_hint: The EU's digital chief frames technological independence and AI safety rules as linked goals.
notes: MLex paywalled; its public description read. Not certain that MLex and European Newsroom interviews are the same sitting (both 9 Oct), so the entry credits each separately.
